expectations.text: Applies the reasoning to Python/backend (does NOT give React- or hook-specific advice)
expectations.evidence: FastAPI-framed throughout: 'routes.py', 'discounts.py — no FastAPI, no DB', 'queries.py get_orders_for_customer(session, ...)'. No React/hook advice.

expectations.text: Recommends a real abstraction (pure function / service / repository) over reflexive file-splitting
expectations.evidence: 'prefer extracting a well-named function or class over relocating code ... an abstraction like calculate_discount() or OrderRepository.get_for_customer() actually reduces the context'.

expectations.text: Co-locates tightly coupled handler+logic; separates only cleanly-standalone layers (e.g. discount calc or DB access)
expectations.evidence: 'Keep the route handlers and their Pydantic models together ... tightly coupled'; thin queries kept inline, only chunky/reusable queries extracted, discount pulled out.

expectations.text: Applies the understood-in-isolation test and/or the ~300-line guidance to the module
expectations.evidence: 'can this be understood in isolation?' and 'The real ceiling is around ~300 lines; past that, signal-to-noise genuinely drops'.
